summary: Minimal self-improving agent loop: AI reads a training script, proposes a change, runs a time-boxed experiment, keeps the change if validation improves, repeats indefinitely. Achieved 700 experiments over 2 days with 20 stacked improvements.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — the self-improving RL loop pattern is explicitly red-flagged in AgentForge's evaluation criteria; also targets ML training pipelines rather than software development orchestration. AgentForge's distillation system already captures run learnings without a live RL loop.

source: DARWIN: Dynamic Agentically Rewriting Self-Improving Network
summary: Genetic-algorithm-style multi-agent system where GPT agents mutate each other's training code; uses persistent JSON memory to correlate changes with model performance improvements. Accepted at ICLR 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — targets ML model training optimization via evolutionary mutation loops, not software development orchestration. The genetic algorithm + RL training loop pattern is explicitly red-flagged in AgentForge's selection criteria.

source: AlphaLab: Autonomous Multi-Agent Research Across Optimization Domains
summary: Autonomous research harness with Strategist/Worker multi-agent loop and a persistent 'playbook' for domain knowledge accumulation. Achieves 4.4x faster CUDA kernels and 22% lower pretraining loss vs single-shot baselines.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the persistent playbook pattern maps to AgentForge's skill distillation system (already shipped). The Strategist/Worker loop maps to existing planner/executor stages. New ideas (adversarial evaluation framework construction, domain knowledge accumulation) would require multi-agent parallelism and external GPU orchestration, both out of AgentForge's current scope.

source: LangGraph Durable Checkpointing (v0.3 + AWS DynamoDB integration)
summary: LangGraph v0.3 adds native DAG workflows and durable checkpointing at each superstep, with a new DynamoDBSaver connector for production-grade state persistence. Enables resume from last checkpoint instead of restart-from-zero on failure.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — maps to AgentForge's open stage-level partial retry gap. However, HID-186 already tracks 'feat(orchestrator): add stage-level partial retry via earliest-failure-point detection'. Theme fully covered; no new issue needed.

source: Anthropic Dreaming — async memory consolidation for Claude Managed Agents
summary: Async 'dreaming' process runs between agent sessions: reviews 1-100 prior sessions, merges duplicate memories, replaces stale entries, surfaces new insights into a curated output memory store. Shipped May 6, 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly relevant to AgentForge's cross-run memory consolidation gap. The dreaming pattern (batch-consolidate, deduplicate, surface insights) would strengthen the existing distillation system. However, HID-188 already tracks 'feat(agents): inject cross-run episodic memory into planner and executor prompts', which covers this theme. The dreaming paper strengthens the case for HID-188 but doesn't justify a separate issue.

source: Skill-SD: Skill-Conditioned Self-Distillation for Multi-turn LLM Agents
summary: Framework that summarizes completed trajectories into compact natural language skills describing successful behaviors, mistakes, and workflows; these skills are then used as training-time supervision for the next iteration. Outperforms vanilla GRPO by +14% on AppWorld.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — the skill-summarization pattern maps closely to AgentForge's existing distillation system and the known gap that executor prompts don't receive distilled skills (only planner does). However, HID-188 tracks injecting episodic memory into both planner and executor prompts, which covers the executor skill injection gap. No separate issue needed.

source: A2A (Agent-to-Agent) Protocol — Linux Foundation standard, CrewAI v1.10.1
summary: Open HTTP-based standard for agent discovery, task exchange, and streaming across frameworks. Google donated to Linux Foundation; backed by Anthropic, Microsoft, Salesforce, 150+ orgs. CrewAI v1.10.1 adds native A2A support as first-class delegation primitive.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses CLI subprocesses (not HTTP-based agent services) as its execution model. Adopting A2A would require a fundamental architectural shift from ProcessRunner/subprocess model to HTTP service agents, which is explicitly out of scope. The inter-agent communication model in AgentForge is deterministic state machine transitions, not dynamic peer-to-peer delegation.

source: LangMem SDK — long-term memory primitives for LangGraph agents
summary: SDK providing semantic (facts/knowledge), episodic (past experiences), and procedural (behavioral rules) memory types for LangGraph agents. Deprecated legacy langchain.memory classes; now canonical memory layer for LangGraph.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the three-tier memory model (semantic/episodic/procedural) is an interesting framing for AgentForge's skill system. AgentForge currently ships semantic/procedural (distilled skills) but lacks episodic (per-run outcome memory). Fully covered by HID-188.
